rv.q: Actress Talia Langman not only plays Ginsburg to perfection, but her physical resemblance is uncanny.
It's still a play I can recommend—its powerful coda, especially, is outstanding—but it could have been much more.

Deering captures Ginsburg’s wit, humor and intelligence as she fights constant mid-century battles for female equality in law school, Big Law, judicial hiring practices and even in her own Jewish faith.
For theater lovers who love plays that rattle their cage, present a teaching moment, or stir their soul, you might find Deering's script a no-news-here 90 minutes, in this writer's view.
But, in erasing the complications of the woman at the heart of the story, the play does its heroine an, um, injustice.

This exceptional, highly imaginative “touching dream” play is filled with flashbacks and flashforwards that provide a glimpse into the worldview of this remarkable “Lady Justice” while it establishes the roots of her pioneering achievements in furthering women’s rights and gender parity.

cn.t: This world premiere about RBG's life and legacy features inventive staging and a strong lead performance, but critics find the play itself uneven—an entertaining yet sentimental treatment that sticks to her public story while leaving deeper elements unexplored.
